arxiv-1802-04109.title: Analysis of Complex System Development Based on Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping
arxiv-1802-04109.creator: Ismail Kayali
arxiv-1802-04109.description: Abstract This article represents one of the contemporary trends in the application of the latest methods of classification in business, where intense competition and the desire to expand drive this science to far-reaching prospects using the discusses months and the most recent classification and forecasting algorithms such as SVM, FFM, C4.

arxiv-2110-05855.title: MoRS: An Approximate Fault Mo delling Framework for R educed-Voltage S RAMs
arxiv-2110-05855.creator: İsmail Emir Yüksel 3 , Behzad Salami 2 , Oğuz Ergin 3 , Osman S. Ünsal 2 , Adrián Cristal Kestelman 2 4
arxiv-2110-05855.description: Abstract On-chip memory (usually based on Static RAMs-SRAMs) are crucial components for various computing devices including heterogeneous devices, e.g, GPUs, FPGAs, ASICs to achieve high performance. Modern workloads such as Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) running on these heterogeneous fabrics are highly dependent on the on-chip memory architecture for efficient acceleration.

arxiv-2112-07770.title: Replication of SARS-CoV-2 mutation analysis suggests differences in per-protein mutation characteristics
arxiv-2112-07770.creator: William Svoboda, Brendan McManamon, Sara Schwartz
arxiv-2112-07770.description: Abstract The increasing spread of COVID-19, caused by the virus SARS-CoV-2, raises concerns about the extent to which mutations have occurred across the viral genome. We present a partial replication of an earlier 2021 study by Wang, R. et al. that determined the presence of four substrains and eleven top mutations in the United States.

arxiv-2212-03841.title: Existence and structure of solutions for general P P -area minimizing surfaces
arxiv-2212-03841.creator: Amir Moradifam, Alexander Rowell
arxiv-2212-03841.description: Abstract We study existence and structure of solutions to the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary problems associated with minimizers of the functional I ⁡ ( u ) = ∫ Ω ( φ ⁡ ( x , D ​ u + F ) + H ​ u ) ​ 𝑑 x I(u)=\int_{\Omega}({\varphi}(x,Du+F)+Hu)\,dx , where φ ⁡ ( x , ξ ) {\varphi}(x,\xi)

arxiv-2305-09882.title: Measuring μ \mu -Distortions from the Thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
arxiv-2305-09882.creator: David Zegeye, Thomas Crawford, Wayne Hu
arxiv-2305-09882.description: Abstract The thermal Sunyaev-Zel’dovich (tSZ) effect is a spectral distortion of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) resulting from inverse Compton scattering of CMB photons with electrons in the medium of galaxy clusters. The spectrum of the tSZ effect is typically calculated assuming the spectrum of the CMB is a blackbody.

arxiv-2311-01834.title: Fermi -LAT detection of the supernova remnant G312.4 − - 0.4 in the vicinity of 4FGL J1409.1 − - 6121e
arxiv-2311-01834.creator: Pauline Chambery, Marianne Lemoine-Goumard, Armelle Jardin-Blicq, Atreyee Sinha, J. Eagle
arxiv-2311-01834.description: Abstract Gamma-ray emission provides constraints on the non-thermal radiation processes at play in astrophysical particle accelerators. This allows both the nature of accelerated particles and the maximum energy that they can reach to be determined. Notably, it remains an open question to what extent supernova remnants (SNRs) contribute to the sea of Galactic cosmic rays.

arxiv-2312-12136.title: Primordial Black Hole Sterile Neutrinogenesis: Sterile Neutrino Dark Matter Production Independent of Couplings Preprint: KEK-QUP-2023-0035, KEK-TH-2584, KEK-Cosmo-0334, IPMU23-0049
arxiv-2312-12136.creator: Muping Chen, Graciela B. Gelmini, Philip Lu, and Volodymyr Takhistov
arxiv-2312-12136.description: Abstract Sterile neutrinos ( ν s \nu_{s} s) are well-motivated and actively searched for hypothetical neutral particles that would mix with the Standard Model active neutrinos. They are considered prime warm dark matter (DM) candidates, typically when their mass is in the keV range, although they can also be hot or cold DM components.

arxiv-2405-16179.title: Network reduction and absence of Hopf Bifurcations in dual phosphorylation networks with three Intermediates
arxiv-2405-16179.creator: Elisenda Feliu and Nidhi Kaihnsa
arxiv-2405-16179.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Elisenda Feliu and Nidhi Kaihnsa. Phosphorylation networks, representing the mechanisms by which proteins are phosphorylated at one or multiple sites, are ubiquitous in cell signalling and display rich dynamics such as unlimited multistability. Dual-site phosphorylation networks are known to exhibit oscillations in the form of periodic trajectories, when phosphorylation and dephosphorylation occurs as a mixed mechanism: phosphorylation of the two sites requires one encounter of the kinase, while dephosphorylation of the two sites requires two encounters with the phosphatase.

arxiv-2406-14170.title: Compact fermionic quantum state preparation with a natural-orbitalizing variational quantum eigensolving scheme
arxiv-2406-14170.creator: P. Besserve, M. Ferrero, T. Ayral
arxiv-2406-14170.description: Abstract Assemblies of strongly interacting fermions, whether in a condensed-matter or a quantum chemistry context, range amongst the most promising candidate systems for which quantum computing platforms could provide an advantage. Near-term quantum state preparation is typically realized by means of the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) algorithm.

arxiv-2408-09246.title: Time Efficient Rate Feedback Tracking Controller with Slew Rate and Control Constraint
arxiv-2408-09246.creator: Seungyeop Han, Byeong-Un Jo, and Koki Ho
arxiv-2408-09246.description: Abstract This paper proposes a time-efficient attitude-tracking controller considering the slew rate constraint and control constraint. The algorithm defines the sliding surface, which is the linear combination of command, body, and regulating angular velocity, and utilizes the sliding surface to derive the control command that guarantees finite time stability.

arxiv-2410-19301.title: “Any Other Thoughts, Hedgehog?” Linking Deliberation Chains in Collaborative Dialogues
arxiv-2410-19301.creator: Abhijnan Nath, Videep Venkatesha, Mariah Bradford, Avyakta Chelle
arxiv-2410-19301.description: Abstract Question-asking in collaborative dialogue has long been established as key to knowledge construction, both in internal and collaborative problem solving. In this work, we examine probing questions in collaborative dialogues: questions that explicitly elicit responses from the speaker’s interlocutors.

arxiv-2503-10071.title: Advanced Tool Learning and Selection System (ATLASS): A Closed-Loop Framework Using LLM
arxiv-2503-10071.creator: Mohd Ariful Haque 1 , Justin Williams 2 , Sunzida Siddique 3, Md. Hujaifa Islam 4 , Hasmot Ali 5 , Kishor Datta Gupta 6 , Roy George 7
arxiv-2503-10071.description: Abstract The combination of LLM agents with external tools enables models to solve complex tasks beyond their knowledge base. Human-designed tools are inflexible and restricted to solutions within the scope of pre-existing tools created by experts. To address this problem, we propose ATLASS, an advanced tool learning and selection system designed as a closed-loop framework.

arxiv-2505-14608.title: Attacks on Machine-Text Detectors Retain Stylistic Fingerprints
arxiv-2505-14608.creator: Rafael A, Rivera Soto, Barry Chen, Nicholas Andrews
arxiv-2505-14608.description: Abstract Despite considerable progress in the development of machine-text detectors, the ease with which machine-text can be manipulated to evade detection has led to suggestions that the problem is inherently intractable. In this work, we investigate the limits of such evasion strategies.

arxiv-2507-05727.title: ContextASR-Bench: A Massive Contextual Speech Recognition Benchmark
arxiv-2507-05727.creator: He Wang, Linhan Ma, Dake Guo, Xiong Wang, Lei Xie, Jin Xu, Junyang Lin
arxiv-2507-05727.description: Abstract Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has been extensively investigated, yet prior evaluative efforts have largely been restricted to contextless paradigms. This constraint stems from the limited proficiency of conventional ASR models in context modeling and their deficiency in memory and reasoning based on world knowledge.

pmc-10540725.title: Risk factors for the development of interstitial lung disease following severe COVID-19 pneumonia and outcomes of systemic corticosteroid therapy: 3-month follow-up
pmc-10540725.creator: Sibel Günay, İzzet Selçuk Parlak, Habibe Hezer, Ebru Şengül Şeref Parlak, Melike Sanem Umut, Zeynep Hancıoğlu, Hülya Çelenk Ergüden, Yasin Kocaman, Aynil Dalkıran, Ümran Sertçelik, İrem Şerifoğlu, Esmehan Akpınar, Muhammed Furkan Göktaş, Meltem Fidan, Büşra Babahanoğlu, Fatma Sinem Cander, Esra Çıvg
pmc-10540725.description: Background:We aimed to evaluate the pulmonary involvement status, its related factors, and pulmonary function test (PFT) results in the first month follow up in patients who were discharged for severe Covid-19 pneumonia; and to assess the efficacy of corticosteroid treatment on these parameters in severe pulmonary involvement patients.

pmc-10605204.title: Child Attachment Representations and Parenting Stress in Mothers and Fathers of School-Age Children with a Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Pilot Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-10605204.creator: Michele Giannotti, Paola Venuti, Simona De Falco
pmc-10605204.description: Mothers and fathers of autistic children (ASD) tend to report elevated levels of parenting stress. Thus, it is critically important to understand which factors contribute to an imbalance between the perceived demands of parenting and the available psychological resources. To date, little is known about the association between child attachment representations and parenting stress.

pmc-10752805.title: Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and the Intestinal Microbiome: An Inseparable Link
pmc-10752805.creator: Maria Effenberger, Christoph Grander, Felix Grabherr, Herbert Tilg
pmc-10752805.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) particularly affects patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity. The incidence of NAFLD has increased significantly over the last decades and is now pandemically across the globe. It is a complex systemic disease comprising hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, lipotoxicity, gut dysbiosis, and insulin resistance as main features and with the potential to progress to cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

pmc-12619180.title: Pilot study of 18F-FAPI-RGD PET/CT for the diagnosis of connective tissue disease associated interstitial lung disease
pmc-12619180.creator: Hao Liu, Xing He, Hui Fang, Nan Liu, Liqing Yang, Caiyu Jiang, Wubin Long, Wei Zhang, Lu Guo
pmc-12619180.description: Background18F-FAPI-RGD PET/CT is a dual-target tracer imaging technique that holds promise for identifying pulmonary lesions in connective tissue disease-associated interstitial lung disease (CTD-ILD) patients. Currently, clinical studies investigating 18F-FAPI-RGD PET/CT for CTD-ILD diagnosis are lacking.MethodsIn this prospective study, CTD-ILD patients from the multidisciplinary clinic of Sichuan Provincial People’s Hospital were enrolled. General clinical data and laboratory parameters were collected.

pmc-12650644.title: Combined Effects of Diazoxide and Moderate-Intensity Exercise on the Restoration of Redox Balance Post-Fatigue in Fast- and Slow-Twitch Skeletal Muscles of Hypertensive Rats
pmc-12650644.creator: Estefanía Bravo-Sánchez, César J Nolasco-Ruiz, Sarai Sánchez-Duarte, Mariana Gómez-Barroso, Manuel Alejandro Vargas-Vargas, Christian Cortés-Rojo, Salvador Manzo-Ávalos, Elizabeth Sánchez-Duarte, Alain Raimundo Rodríguez-Orozco, Alfredo Saavedra-Molina, Rocío Montoya-Pérez
pmc-12650644.description: Simple SummaryMuscle fatigue is linked to redox imbalance and worsens under hypertension due to oxidative stress. This study tested whether diazoxide and moderate exercise could protect skeletal muscles in hypertensive rats after a fatigue protocol. Hypertension increased oxidants and reduced antioxidant defenses. Both interventions, when used alone or in combination, improved antioxidant activity and reduced oxidant levels.

pmc-13388023.title: Microbial Profile Alteration as a Potential Biomarker and Therapeutic Target in Children with Celiac Disease: A Narrative Review
pmc-13388023.creator: Fahimeh Sadat Mostafaei, Nikoo Hossein-Khannazer, Somayeh Jahani Sherafat, Asal Noruzpur, Amir Sadeghi, Mohammad Rostami Nejad
pmc-13388023.description: Celiac disease (CD) is an autoimmune disorder triggered by gluten ingestion in genetically susceptible individuals. While gluten exposure is a necessary environmental trigger, its interaction with the intestinal microbiota has recently been recognized as a critical factor in modulating the onset and progression of the disease.

pmc-13455860.creator: Andrew Corley, Claire Dunn, Yuen Wai Hung, Andrea Sprockett, Dominic Montagu, Nirali Chakraborty
pmc-13455860.description: This commentary outlines 4 practical lessons derived from analyzing a country-specific measure of wealth available for use in 68 countries, serving as axioms for development practitioners to simplify questions related to identifying relative poverty and project design and implementation. INTRODUCTION Human development indicators and socioeconomics are tightly intertwined.
